IR.rationale: A rising 1Y-FedFunds spread signals that markets are pricing tighter policy. That raises funding costs and pressures leveraged and carry-type hedge-fund positions.

B.rationale: High-yield and EM corporate yields rising together mark a broad credit sell-off. That hurts credit-sensitive strategies (distressed, event driven, convertible arbitrage) and tightens prime-broker financing.

V.rationale: Volatility driven by financial-crisis news marks a deleveraging regime, in which liquidity-providing hedge-fund strategies underperform.

AP.rationale: Strong US and EM equity markets together mark a risk-on state. Most hedge-fund indices carry positive market beta and benefit from such states with some lag.

TF.rationale: High payoffs on short-rate trend straddles indicate large interest-rate moves. Such moves are associated with dislocations that hurt arbitrage and macro positioning.

ST.rationale: A flight to quality combined with weak reversal profits indicates scarce liquidity provision and crowded unwinds. That is a poor state for equity long/short and market-neutral books.

FX.rationale: A broadly weaker dollar alongside a firm commodity-carry currency signals easy global funding and risk appetite. That supports hedge-fund returns.

COM.rationale: Rising copper reflects improving global growth expectations, which are favourable for risk-bearing strategies.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions with weak activity mark a funding-constrained, slowing economy. In that state leveraged strategies earn less.

ENDG.rationale: Hedge-fund returns are serially correlated because of illiquid holdings and return smoothing, so strong recent performance tends to persist.

IR.rationale: Rising bill rates mean tighter short-term funding. That raises the risk of forced deleveraging and large drawdowns.

B.rationale: Simultaneous jumps in Euro high-yield and EM corporate yields signal a global credit shock. These shocks are the classic trigger of hedge-fund tail losses.

V.rationale: High equity volatility driven by financial-crisis concerns marks the stress regime in which hedge-fund losses cluster.

AP.rationale: Weak US and EM equities together indicate a risk-off state. Short-option-like hedge-fund exposures then face elevated tail risk.

TF.rationale: Large short-rate trend payoffs flag violent rate moves that can dislocate fixed-income arbitrage and macro positions.

ST.rationale: A flight to quality with failing reversal profits indicates liquidity withdrawal and crowded unwinds, which precede large losses.

FX.rationale: A strengthening dollar tightens global dollar funding and is associated with risk-off episodes and carry unwinds.

COM.rationale: Falling oil and copper together signal a global demand slowdown. That raises downside risk across event-driven and macro books.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions combined with weak real activity is the macro state most associated with hedge-fund drawdowns.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent performance tends to persist through smoothing and redemption-driven deleveraging, which raises the chance of further large losses.

IR.rationale: Falling expectations of tighter policy ease funding conditions and support strong rebounds.

B.rationale: Falling EM and high-yield yields indicate a credit rally. Such rallies produce outsized gains for distressed, event-driven and credit-arbitrage strategies.

V.rationale: Elevated volatility raises dispersion and the opportunity set. Trend followers can profit strongly, and post-stress rebounds can produce large gains.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equities reflect global risk appetite, which feeds into large hedge-fund gains given their positive beta.

TF.rationale: Calm short-rate markets allow carry and arbitrage strategies to harvest premia without disruption.

ST.rationale: The absence of a flight to quality means risk appetite toward weaker firms. That benefits event-driven and long-biased equity strategies.

FX.rationale: A risk-on, weak-dollar state with a strong commodity currency eases global funding and favours large gains.

COM.rationale: Rising copper signals reflation and growth momentum, which accompanies strong risk-asset rallies.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress often precedes sharp recoveries in which illiquidity premia are recaptured, so it raises the chance of large gains as well as losses.

ENDG.rationale: Return persistence in hedge-fund indices means strong recent performance raises the probability of a further large gain.
